1. Core Clinical Tension: An immunocompetent young woman with chronic back pain experiences progressive vertebral destruction, endplate collapse, and bilateral giant psoas abscesses despite 16 months of empiric first-line antituberculous therapy, highlighting treatment failure caused by occult multidrug resistance in spinal infection.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Outpatient evaluation upon presenting with treatment failure, including 18-month symptom chronology, prior first-line medication history, physical exam (dorso-lumbar tenderness, motion restriction), baseline laboratory testing (mild anemia, elevated ESR/CRP, non-reactive HIV, negative sputum smear/culture), plain radiographs, and repeat MRI demonstrating L1 collapse and bilateral psoas collections, stopping strictly before psoas pus aspiration, CBNAAT/GeneXpert rifampicin resistance detection, and liquid culture DST.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis (e.g. Staphylococcus aureus) causes vertebral collapse and psoas collections but typically presents with acute high fever, leukocytosis, and rapid progression. Spinal malignancy (metastasis/multiple myeloma) causes vertebral collapse with pedicle involvement but typically spares the intervertebral disc and lacks large, cold psoas abscess collections.
case_prompt:
A 33-year-old married Indian woman from a low socioeconomic background presents to the outpatient clinic with a chronic backache persisting for 18 months. The pain began insidiously, initially intermittent for three months, but subsequently became continuous and disabling. Over the preceding 16 months, she received an extended empiric antimicrobial regimen (a fixed-dose combination of isoniazid, pyrazinamide, rifampicin, and ethambutol for 56 days, followed by isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol for 14 months) for presumed drug-sensitive spinal infection; however, her back pain progressively intensified. She denies cough, night sweats, fevers, anorexia, weight loss, traumatic injury, heavy lifting, personal or family contact with known infectious diseases, substance misuse, or incarceration.

On physical examination, she is afebrile with a body mass index of 21.6 kg/m2. Examination of the spine demonstrates marked tenderness across the dorso-lumbar region with severe limitation of spinal motion when bending or rising from bed. Neurological, pulmonary, and cardiovascular examinations are entirely normal.

Laboratory studies reveal a hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, total leukocyte count of 5,800/mm3 (71% polymorphonuclear cells, 19% lymphocytes), erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 63 mm/hr, and C-reactive protein of 21 mg/L. Serologic screening for HIV types I and II is non-reactive. Sputum direct smear and mycobacterial cultures are negative. A plain radiograph of the lumbar spine reveals bony destruction involving the inferior endplate of L1 and the superior endplate of L2, while a plain chest radiograph is unremarkable. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the dorso-lumbar spine demonstrates significant collapse of the L1 vertebral body with cortical destruction and marrow edema, partial collapse of D12 with loss of D12-L1 intervertebral height, mild bone marrow edema in D11 and L2, pre- and paravertebral collections, and bilateral large psoas abscesses measuring 27 x 57 mm on the right and 25 x 12 mm on the left with mild retropulsion of L1.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Spondylodiscitis (e.g., Staphylococcal or Gram-Negative)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to progressive destructive discitis and large psoas abscesses, but ruled out by an afebrile 18-month chronic indolent clinical course, normal systemic leukocyte count, and sterile routine bacterial evaluations.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: There was no history of coughing, loss of weight, loss of appetite, night sweats, or fever... A detailed clinical examination revealed an afebrile woman... laboratory evaluation showed a hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dl and a total leucocyte count of 5800/mm3

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to pathological compression fracture of L1 and localized bone destruction, but contiguous involvement across the D12-L1 intervertebral disc space with endplate erosions and extensive cold psoas abscesses favored an infectious granulomatous process rather than tumor metastasis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Further investigations, including a radiograph of the lumbar region, showed destruction at the lower shelf of L1 and the upper shelf of L2... partial collapse of D12 with a loss of D12-L1 height with inferior endplate erosion... There were large psoas abscesses on the right (27 x 57 mm) and left (25 x 12 mm).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Ultrasound-guided aspiration of the psoas abscess with cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification test (CBNAAT) detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis with rifampicin resistance, and automated liquid culture and line probe assay confirmed high-level isoniazid (katG) and rifampicin co-resistance, establishing multidrug-resistant tuberculosis of the spine.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: her cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification of the pus was positive with medium detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with resistance to rifampicin. Another sample sent for liquid automated culture was suggestive of the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid. A line probe assay after inoculation into liquid culture was suggestive of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid (high level to the katG gene).

editor_comments: Admission clinical presentation isolates the clinical failure of first-line therapy before CBNAAT and drug susceptibility testing. Zero pathogen names in prompt. Exact verbatim quotes from article included.
